newsitem.title: BRAZIL: COFFEE--Brazil blossoms do not lift growers' hopes.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE--Brazil blossoms do not lift growers' hopes.

text.p: Brazil's coffee farmers are looking ahead to 1997/98 and based on current flowerings, very early signs are that output in key states will be below this year, according to a Reuters' survey of cooperatives.
Actual forecasts can only really start to be made in November when the flowers have begun setting, giving agronomists a more concrete idea of crop size.
But the fact most regions will see an "off" year in the cycle where there is a larger harvest every other year means even at this early stage, agronomists expect a drop in output.

"I certainly believe next year's harvest will be lower than this year's which I would put at 24 million to 25 million 60-kg bags," said Manoel Bertone, vice-president of the growers' National Coffee Council and president of Garca cooperative.
Others predict falls of up to 50 percent in regions that have been hit by dry weather such as Espirito Santo and the Zona da Mata region in Minas Gerais.

"I'm expecting a 30 percent drop overall so if you expected a crop this year of around 27.5 million bags, then you could be talking about 19 million bags," said Mauricio Miarelli, agronomist at the Franca co-operative in north Sao Paulo state.
Other traders are considering a worst/best case scenario of 21 million to 24 million bags, although caution it is still too early to talk about crop size with any degree of confidence.

The outlook is not so grim for all states, with producers in Parana and Bahia both hoping to see an increase in output. But given both states' contribution to overall production, any rise will not make up for shortfalls elsewhere, traders said.

One other positive sign this year is that after a crop in which there was no offical government survey, producers are hopeful technicians from the Agriculture and Industry and Commerce Ministries may have an estimate by end-November.
Comments from co-operatives in key states follow.

* Guaxupe - small flowering at the beginning of September, with second, probably major, flowering in the penultimate week of last month. Still expecting a third, smaller blooming however. Output expected down from last year. * Varginha - two flowerings already, one after rains earlier in September and one at start of this week. Still harvesting 20 percent of 1996/97 crop due to delays caused by labor and rain. Already forecasting fall from this year's 500,000 bags.

* Cerrado (Centre for Coffee Co-operatives) - one medium-sized flowering took place September 21-24, this likely to be main flowering. Already anticipating possible 40 percent drop in 1996/97 harvest of 3.2 million bags, including production from new trees coming onstream. * Caratinga (Zona da Mata) - one small flowering so far. Area hit by dry weather plus trees in the region likely to be tired from producing larger crop than usual this year of around 2.5 million bags. Total Zona da Mata output could drop by up to 50 percent or at most reach 1.5 million bags.

In SAO PAULO, cooperatives in the north such as Franca have seen two small flowerings so far which have only taken place on younger plants and higher branches of older ones. This is better than in the southwest where, for example in Garca, there has only been one, not very good flowering.
In ESPIRITO SANTO, gloomiest predictions are of a drop of up to 50 percent because of dry weather, with some traders working on a worst/best case scenario of between 3.8 million and 4.2 million bags.

PARANA and BAHIA are both expected to see higher output, particularly Parana where trees planted in 1994, the year of the two frosts, should start production, boosting the crop possibly to two million bags from one million to 1.2 million this year.
In Bahia, a delayed flowering in March this year means that growers will in the next three months still be harvesting a large part of the 1996/97 crop.
However the main flowering in 1997/98 should take place in January/February, with hopes of a crop of one million bags against this year's 800,000 bags.
